description: Pre-registered attempts to fit and validate process components and model families on the normalized datasets published in this catalog. Splits, loader options, vintage policies and acceptance criteria are frozen here BEFORE any holdout result is read. A failing attempt is a result: it is kept, not re-specified. A change after seeing test outcomes must be added as a new attempt with a new id, a reason, and the superseded attempt left in place.
rules: Splits are chosen from data coverage only (first and last available period), never from outcomes.
Acceptance criteria are the component or family defaults declared in requirements.json; no attempt weakens them.
Entity selection rules (issuers, countries, symbols, regions) are declared here and use availability or pre-training-window counts only.

vintage_policy is the weakest policy the loaded sources support. 'retrospective' means timing leakage is controlled by the requirement's publication lag but revision leakage is possible, and the report says so.
Compute budget per attempt: 30 minutes wall clock. An attempt that exceeds it is recorded as not_run with reason compute_budget, not silently dropped.

attempts.data: eia_energy@normalized (PET weekly WCESTUS1, WCRFPUS2, WCRIMUS2, WCREXUS2, WCRRIUS2; subject iso3:USA)
attempts.rationale: Weekly crude balance covers 1991-02 onward (exports are the binding start). Train ends 2015, validation 2016-2019, holdout 2020-2024. EIA bulk records carry only an acquisition timestamp, so the retrospective policy with the declared 5-day publication lag is the only admissible one; the component already allows the 'minor' revision class.
attempts.superseded_reason: Retained with its verdict. Its inputs and its Gaussian in-sample interval are unchanged and its numbers reproduce exactly; v2 changes only the declared predictive distribution.

attempts.data: eia_energy@normalized (MGFUPUS2 monthly, EMM_EPMR_PTE_NUS_DPG weekly) + fred_oil_price@normalized (DCOILWTICO ALFRED vintages)
attempts.rationale: The retail gasoline price starts 1990-08, so the aligned monthly sample starts 1990-09. Train 1990-2009, validation 2010-2015, holdout 2016-2024. The crude price carries real ALFRED vintages; the two EIA series do not, so the frame is retrospective.

attempts.data: eia_energy@normalized (EMM_EPMR_PTE_NUS_DPG, WGTSTUS1 weekly) + fred_oil_price@normalized (DCOILWTICO)
attempts.rationale: Same sample and splits as demand_price_elasticity: the two components share the retail price series and must not be split differently.

attempts.entity_rule: The five issuers with the most published companyfacts records across all four required concepts (CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue, Revenues, CostsAndExpenses, PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment), ranked by the smallest per-concept record count and then by CIK. Availability only: no fit or forecast was run before this list was frozen.
attempts.data: sec_company_assets@normalized (companyfacts; observed_at is the filing date)
attempts.rationale: companyfacts carries filing dates as knowledge time, so the strict policy is admissible. Quarters are labeled by the calendar quarter containing the fiscal period end; fourth-quarter flows are derived as the annual duration minus the three reported quarters.

attempts.data: census_population@normalized (PEP vintages 2020-2024, subject geo:US, July 1 estimates)
attempts.rationale: PEP vintages carry release dates, so availability is real-time. Coverage is 2010-2024 (15 annual points), which is short: the component needs 8 observations to fit and 8 holdout forecasts, so at most 7 origins can exist. The attempt is run anyway to record the outcome honestly; a longer real-time series (POPTHM vintages) would be needed to pass.

attempts.data: ucdp_conflicts@normalized (GED monthly country counts, release 26.1, state-based) + vdem@normalized (v2x_polyarchy, previous year)
attempts.entity_rule: The 20 countries with the most state-based GED events in 2000-01..2015-12 (the training window only).
attempts.rationale: Hawkes self- and neighbour-excitation on country-month counts. No contiguity dataset (CShapes) is published, so neighbours are omitted and the neighbour term is identified only from the panel. UCDP annual releases revise earlier months, and the row dates are event months rather than publication dates, so no_revision_leakage is expected to fail; that is recorded rather than excused.
attempts.correction: 2026-09-15: the split boundaries were first written as YYYY-MM (2015-12, 2019-12, 2024-12), which validate_process rejects ("Invalid time"). They are rewritten as the identical end-of-month dates. The windows are unchanged and no result had been produced when this was corrected.

attempts.data: alpaca_daily_bars@normalized (adjusted daily closes) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF as the daily risk-free rate)
attempts.entity_rule: Five mega-cap issuers from distinct sectors declared in advance (AAPL, MSFT, JNJ, XOM, KO); SPY is the market factor and is never scored.
attempts.rationale: The holdout needs supplied factors, so the market factor is SPY's excess return over DFF/252; the scored symbols are not in the factor. Total-return adjusted closes are restated by later corporate actions, so revisions are declared 'minor' and no_revision_leakage is expected to fail; the skill criteria (CRPS against constant volatility, DM against the historical mean) are still informative.

attempts.data: eia_energy@normalized (weekly crude stocks, production, imports, exports, refiner net input) + fred_oil_price@normalized (DCOILWTICO weekly mean)
attempts.rationale: The weekly U.S. crude balance is the family's own declared data source. Flows in thousand barrels per day are converted to thousand barrels per week; refiner net input stands in for consumption and net imports are imports minus exports, so the published balance discrepancy is reported rather than hidden.

attempts.data: census_business@normalized (County Business Patterns employment by state and NAICS sector)
attempts.rationale: CBP state-by-sector employment is published for 2019-2023 only. Base-year shares are 2019, the validation target is 2022 and the holdout target is 2023 (51 state forecasts). QCEW (bls_labor) would give a longer panel.
attempts.superseded_reason: Retained with its verdict. v2 changes only the declared predictive spread (per-unit instead of pooled).

delinquency_rate.description: Constructed: 100 * sum(bank_noncurrent_loans) / sum(bank_net_loans) over all FDIC-insured banks in the quarter. Substitutes for the declared FRED DRCCLACBS credit-card delinquency rate, which is not published locally; requirements.json names FDIC call reports as the bank-panel alternative.

unemployment_rate.description: Constructed: 100 * sum(unemployed) / sum(labor_force) over the 51 seasonally adjusted LAUS state series. bls_labor publishes no national CPS rate (LNS14000000 is absent from this build).

attempts.data: fdic_bank_financials@normalized + bls_labor@normalized + fred_policy_rate@normalized, quarterly 2010Q1 onward
attempts.rationale: The unemployment input was the blocker; LAUS state levels now make a national rate constructible, and the FDIC aggregate noncurrent-loan rate stands in for the unpublished credit-card delinquency series. FDIC call reports and LAUS carry no vintages, so the policy is retrospective with the declared 50-day publication lag; the component already allows the 'minor' revision class. Both substitutions are overrides recorded here and visible in the estimate's data audit. Train 2010Q1-2017Q4, validation 2018-2020, holdout 2021-2025.
attempts.expected_limits: The noncurrent-loan rate of all bank loans is a different object from a credit-card delinquency rate; a pass would say the hazard mechanism tracks aggregate loan distress, not consumer default.
attempts.superseded_reason: DRCCLACBS and UNRATE are now published with ALFRED vintages, so the primary series can be used under the strict real-time policy. This attempt and its pass are kept as the record of what the substituted series produced. Already superseded by default_hazard.fred_primary_realtime for using substitute series; ALSO superseded on data version, because bls_labor@50917b81 was an incomplete download holding about 30% of the rows.

attempts.data: fred_cpi@normalized (CPIAUCSL ALFRED vintages) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF vintages) + bls_labor@normalized (LAUS states)
attempts.rationale: fred_cpi now carries full ALFRED vintages, so inflation is read point-in-time: month t uses its first release and the base month t-12 uses the latest vintage available at that release. The policy rate is the monthly mean of first-published DFF. The output gap is the declared blocker: GDPC1 and GDPPOT are unpublished, so the attempt uses an Okun proxy, -2 * (u - u*), with u the constructed LAUS national rate and u* its trailing 120-month mean computed only from earlier months. Train 1990-2007, validation 2008-2014, holdout 2015-2024.
attempts.expected_limits: The gap is a proxy, not the declared GDPC1/GDPPOT gap, and the LAUS unemployment input carries no vintages, so the row set is declared valid_time with major revisions and no_revision_leakage is expected to fail. When fred_macro_panel publishes GDPC1/GDPPOT/UNRATE vintages this attempt should be superseded by a real-time-clean one.
attempts.superseded_reason: GDPC1 and GDPPOT are now published, so the declared output gap replaces the Okun proxy. Already superseded by monetary_model.fred_realtime_quarterly for using an Okun proxy; ALSO superseded on data version (incomplete bls_labor@50917b81).

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (DPRIME) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF), monthly means of daily vintages
attempts.rationale: Both series carry ALFRED vintages, so the strict real-time policy applies and no_revision_leakage is evaluable. DPRIME and DFF entered ALFRED in 2005-06, so the holdout starts well inside the vintage era: train to 2012, validation 2013-2017, holdout 2018-2024 (84 monthly origins).
attempts.superseded_reason: WS-E interval calibration, 2026-09-17: see the sixth_wave note and docs/research-log/ws-e-interval-coverage.md.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (SNDR) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF), monthly
attempts.rationale: SNDR starts 2021-04 (74 vintage records, 65 months). The component needs 36 observations to fit and 24 holdout forecasts, so the series cannot satisfy both; the attempt is run to record that honestly rather than leaving it unattempted. Train 2021-04..2024-03, validation 2024-04..2025-03, holdout 2025-04..2026-08.
attempts.expected_limits: minimum_test_forecasts is expected to fail (at most 17 origins against a declared 24).

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (DRCCLACBS, UNRATE) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF), quarterly
attempts.rationale: The declared primary series with ALFRED vintages, replacing the FDIC/LAUS substitutions of the second wave. DRCCLACBS entered ALFRED in 2011-05, so the holdout sits inside the vintage era: train to 2016, validation 2017-2019, holdout 2020-2025. Same split boundaries as the superseded attempt so the two are comparable.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (DPSACBW027SBOG weekly, month-end) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF)
attempts.rationale: H.8 deposits entered ALFRED in 2012-08, so the strict policy leaves 2013 onward usable: train to 2016, validation 2017-2019, holdout 2020-2024 (60 monthly origins) — which includes the 2020 deposit surge.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (TOTALSL), monthly
attempts.rationale: TOTALSL entered ALFRED in 1996-12. Train to 2004, validation 2005-2012, holdout 2013-2024 (144 monthly origins). AR order is selected by BIC inside each fit, so selection stays inside the training information set.
attempts.contaminated: Read TOTALSL from the build with the billions/millions bug: 11,612 of 13,537 values were wrong by 1000x, which corrupts log growth at every affected vintage boundary. Contaminated.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (RRSFS) + fred_oil_price@normalized (DCOILWTICO) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF)
attempts.rationale: RRSFS entered ALFRED in 2001-06 and DFF in 2005-06, so the binding start is 2005: train to 2012, validation 2013-2017, holdout 2018-2024.
attempts.contaminated: RRSFS values are unchanged, but its unit token became million_USD_1982_1984_cpi_adjusted, so the attempt is re-run to pin the rebuilt inputs. The v1 verdict is expected to stand.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (PAYEMS, INDPRO), monthly
attempts.rationale: Both series have deep ALFRED histories (PAYEMS 1961, INDPRO 1927). Train to 2004, validation 2005-2012, holdout 2013-2024 (144 monthly origins).
attempts.contaminated: INDPRO was rebased 13 times since 1927; in the old build every vintage carried the index_2017_100 label, so growth rates spanning a rebasing were wrong. Contaminated.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (FEDFUNDS, CPIAUCSL, GDPC1, GDPPOT), quarterly
attempts.rationale: All four declared series now carry ALFRED vintages. FEDFUNDS entered ALFRED in 1996-12 and GDPPOT in 1994-01, so the usable real-time span starts 1997: train to 2004, validation 2005-2012, holdout 2013-2024 (48 quarterly origins).
attempts.expected_limits: The component reads GDPC1 and GDPPOT levels directly. ALFRED vintages of chained-dollar series are in the base year current at each vintage while the records carry only the current unit label, so the level gap mixes base years across the 1999, 2013 and 2023 benchmark revisions. The estimate is reported with that caveat; the monetary attempt below measures the gap base-invariantly instead.
attempts.contaminated: Read GDPC1, GDPPOT and CPIAUCSL levels from a build where every vintage carried one unit label, so the within-row output gap and the four-quarter inflation ratio mixed base years across the 1988 CPI rebasing and the 1999/2013/2023 NIPA benchmark revisions. The estimate is contaminated and is retained only as the record of that run.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (FEDFUNDS, GDPC1, GDPPOT) + fred_cpi@normalized (CPIAUCSL), quarterly first releases
attempts.rationale: Supersedes the Okun-proxy attempt: the declared GDPC1/GDPPOT gap replaces it, at the rule's own quarterly frequency (rho is a quarterly smoothing parameter). Every input is its initial release, so no row contains a later revision and revisions are declared 'none'. Rows run 1995Q1-2024Q4 (120 quarters): train to 2007, validation 2008-2014, holdout 2015-2024 (40 quarters).
attempts.expected_limits: The gap is measured relative to its trailing 40-quarter mean inside one point-in-time snapshot, because ALFRED chained-dollar vintages carry no base-year metadata and a raw real-time level ratio produced gaps of +22% at benchmark revisions. A constant base offset cancels in logs; what remains is the gap relative to its recent average, which r_star absorbs. Inflation uses the quarter's first CPI month, the earliest print a real-time observer has.
attempts.contaminated: Built the output gap and inflation from per-period first releases across mixed bases, which forced a trailing-mean demeaning workaround. With per-vintage base_period the ratios are formed inside one base and the gap is a true level, so this pass was obtained on contaminated inputs and is superseded.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (FEDFUNDS, CPIAUCSL, GDPC1, GDPPOT), quarterly
attempts.rationale: Same splits as the contaminated v1 attempt so the two are directly comparable. Base-agnostic selection: the source accepts whatever unit each vintage published and the requirement unit is applied as a label, with the published unit and base kept in attributes.published_unit/base_period. A point-in-time frame takes the latest vintage available at its cutoff for every period, and a vintage publishes its whole history on one base, so each frame is internally base-consistent and the estimator only reads within-frame ratios and growth rates.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (TOTALSL, now billions in every vintage), monthly
attempts.rationale: Same splits as v1; the only change is the corrected TOTALSL values.
attempts.superseded_reason: Retained with its verdict. v3 adds the declared data-revision variance component; nothing else changes.

A point-in-time frame takes the latest vintage available at its cutoff for every period, and a vintage publishes its whole history on one base, so each frame is internally base-consistent and the estimator only reads within-frame ratios and growth rates.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (RRSFS) + fred_oil_price@847b0f93 + fred_policy_rate@2a3197b9, monthly
attempts.rationale: Same splits as v1; re-run only because RRSFS's unit token changed. Values are identical, so the verdict is expected to repeat.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (FEDFUNDS, GDPC1, GDPPOT) + fred_cpi@34fe03f5 (CPIAUCSL), quarterly first releases
attempts.rationale: Same splits as v1. The output gap is now 100*(GDPC1/GDPPOT - 1) with both levels taken from the newest base on which both series had published by the target quarter's first release, and inflation uses one CPI base for both endpoints, so the trailing-mean workaround is gone and the gap is a true level (range -10.8% in 2020Q2 to +4.0%, against -9.7..+9.0 under the workaround and +22.5 before it).

attempts.data: eia_energy@f5cd9308 (PET weekly WCESTUS1, WCRFPUS2, WCRIMUS2, WCREXUS2, WCRRIUS2; subject iso3:USA)
attempts.diagnosis: v1 failed interval_coverage alone (0.640 against 0.80 +/- 0.15) while beating persistence at p = 0.00093. The failure is a static predictive scale against strongly time-varying error volatility, not a too-narrow scale everywhere: over the holdout the mean predictive sd moves only 3,121 -> 3,380 while the realized one-step RMSE moves 4,473 (2020), 3,082 (2021), 6,113 (2022), 5,838 (2023), 3,243 (2024), and yearly coverage is 0.60/0.83/0.42/0.54/0.82. Within the training window the same expanding in-sample Gaussian scale OVER-covers (0.894-0.908 against 0.80) because 1991-1995 residuals (sd 4,563) inflate it relative to 2006-2010 (sd 1,562). Standardized holdout errors also have kurtosis 4.3 and are left-skewed (10% quantile -2.28, 90% +1.09).
attempts.interval_method: empirical_trailing, window 52 weeks, 40 quantile nodes, plus coefficient uncertainty x'Vx. The scale is the root mean square of the last 52 one-step residuals (one year, the petroleum stock cycle), and the shape is the empirical quantiles of residuals standardized by their own trailing scale, so tails and asymmetry are taken from the data rather than assumed. Chosen on training-window evidence only: over 1991-2019 the trailing Gaussian attains 0.789-0.796 coverage and the trailing empirical 0.797-0.808 at a nominal 0.80, against 0.894-0.908 for the expanding in-sample Gaussian.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits, vintage policy and acceptance criteria to inventory_balance.eia_weekly; the predictive distribution is the only change, so the two attempts are directly comparable.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (TOTALSL), monthly
attempts.diagnosis: v2 failed interval_coverage alone (0.596) while beating persistence at p = 0.0022. The scored error is not the error the residuals measure. Under the strict real-time policy the forecast is anchored on the TOTALSL level available at the origin, while the actual is the latest vintage available at the evaluation cutoff, so the scored error contains the anchor level revision. TOTALSL log revisions from first release to latest have sd 0.0177 for 2013+ periods and 0.0348 for 1997-2012 (mean +0.070), against a model residual scale of 0.0057: realized standardized holdout errors have root mean square 3.73, and coverage bunches by year (0.00 in 2016 and 2022, 1.00 in 2014, 2018, 2019 and 2024) rather than scattering, which is the signature of one persistent revision episode per benchmark rather than of model noise. Excess kurtosis is small (3.78), so the tails are not the problem.
attempts.interval_method: gaussian_in_sample residual scale plus an independent data-revision component: the standard deviation of the log revisions the publisher has ALREADY made by the origin, over the most recent 60 mature periods, where mature means at least 12 months old. Twelve months is the shortest age at which a G.19 period has been through one annual benchmark, and five years keeps the estimate inside the current revision regime instead of averaging over the 2000s benchmark that moved the level about 5%. The mean revision is reported but deliberately NOT used to shift the point forecast, so any systematic revision bias stays visible in the bias statistic instead of being absorbed into the mechanism.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits, vintage policy and acceptance criteria to credit_growth.fred_realtime_v2.

attempts.data: census_business@5b0995c7 (County Business Patterns employment by state and NAICS sector)
attempts.diagnosis: v1 failed interval_coverage in the opposite direction (1.000 against 0.80 +/- 0.15) while halving the year-effect-only baseline error at p = 4.1e-06. The predictive sd of 0.0540 decomposes into a pooled within-year residual sd of 0.0201 and a between-year term of 0.0502; the between-year term is the variance of THREE year effects (-0.013, +0.071, +0.050) whose dispersion is the 2020 collapse and the 2021 rebound, added at full size as if the next year were a fresh draw. The within-year part is pooled across states whose own residual sds run from 0.0009 to 0.047, a factor of fifty, so one scale is simultaneously far too wide for stable states and too narrow for volatile ones. Realized 2023 cross-state error sd was 0.0115 with a common component of +0.0078.
attempts.interval_method: per_unit_year_mean: each state gets its own residual mean square shrunk toward the pooled one by a single prior observation (a three-year panel gives each state three residuals), and the common term becomes the sampling variance of the ESTIMATED year level (between-year variance / Y) rather than the variance of a fresh draw. Addresses the pooling defect directly; it cannot repair the common term, which three pandemic-era year effects cannot estimate.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits and acceptance criteria to regional_model.cbp_state_sectors.
attempts.expected_limits: With one holdout year, all 51 forecasts share one draw of the common component, so interval_coverage here is one Bernoulli trial and not a coverage estimate. regional_model.qcew_state_sectors is registered below to make the criterion evaluable on a longer panel with six holdout years. no_revision_leakage fails as in v1: CBP publishes no vintages.
attempts.superseded_reason: WS-E interval calibration, 2026-09-17: see the sixth_wave note and docs/research-log/ws-e-interval-coverage.md.

attempts.data: bls_labor@ffd7f43a (QCEW annual-average private employment, state x NAICS 2-digit sector, aggregation level 54, 2005-2024)
attempts.entity_rule: Every state-equivalent QCEW publishes at aggregation level 54 (50 states, DC and Puerto Rico; 53 areas), and every two-digit NAICS private sector. Selection is availability only.
attempts.rationale: The declared fix for the CBP attempt: the rebuilt bls_labor (60.9M rows) carries QCEW annual averages from 1990, so the panel has twenty years and nineteen growth years instead of four and three. Base-year shares are 2005, the validation targets are 2015-2018 and the holdout is 2019-2024, six years x 53 areas, so the between-year component is estimated from thirteen year effects at the first holdout origin and interval_coverage is evaluated over six independent common draws instead of one. QCEW labels each year with the NAICS revision in force, so two-digit sector codes are compared across revisions and the published namespaces are recorded.
attempts.expected_limits: no_revision_leakage is expected to fail: QCEW is benchmarked annually and bls_labor publishes one current vintage, so row dates are not information times. The holdout deliberately contains 2020 and 2021, which no interval method can anticipate; that is the point of scoring six years rather than one.
attempts.superseded_reason: WS-E interval calibration, 2026-09-17: see the sixth_wave note and docs/research-log/ws-e-interval-coverage.md.

attempts.data: mit_election_returns@017e0d4f (U.S. House district general-election returns 1976-2024) + fec_candidates@a46824fd (candidate master: office, state, district, party, CAND_ICI) + fec@93722c10 (weball candidate cycle receipts) + fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (DSPIC96 ALFRED vintages)
attempts.entity_rule: Every U.S. House district-cycle general election (no primaries, no special elections) for which all declared inputs exist: a two-party result, a partisan lean from a contested result within the previous three cycles, an FEC candidate record for the cycle, and a national income growth reading published on election day. Availability only.
attempts.split_rule: By ELECTION YEAR, so no future election can inform a past prediction: fit through 2016, validate 2018-2020, test 2022-2024. Each holdout origin refits on cycles up to and including the previous one.

district_presidential_lean.source_series: MEDSL U.S. House district returns, previous contested cycle
district_presidential_lean.description: Substitutes for the declared district presidential lean. No published dataset in this catalog provides presidential vote by congressional district: mit_election_returns publishes county and statewide presidential returns, and counties do not nest inside congressional districts. pvi is instead the district two-party Democratic share in its most recent contested cycle within three cycles, minus the national two-party Democratic House share of that same cycle.

fred_economy.description: Substitutes for the declared A229RX0 (real disposable personal income per capita), which fred_macro_panel does not publish. econ is the twelve-month growth of real disposable personal income read from the ALFRED vintage available ON election day, with both endpoints on one base period.

attempts.rationale: The elections family was blocked on data until mit_election_returns published House district returns. The target is the contested district two-party Democratic share in the next cycle given realized fundamentals; the secondary declared group is the Democratic seat count. Baselines: persistence (the district previous share), historical_mean (its pre-origin mean) and the supplied incumbent_party_holds rule (every seat stays with the party holding it, at that party average holding share; for seats, the current split). Acceptance is the family default plus the declared beats_district_mean_dm.
attempts.expected_limits: Three timing caveats are declared rather than hidden. (1) FEC weball receipts are cycle-to-date totals whose coverage ends after election day (2000: 2001-06-30 ... 2024: 2025-01-30), so fundraising is a conditional input: the holdout tests the mechanism given realized fundraising, not the ability to forecast it. (2) Receipts are summed over all of a party candidates in the district-cycle, including primary losers. (3) Redistricting changes what a district number means in 2002, 2012 and 2022, so the lagged lean crosses a boundary change in those cycles; the family already declares this. Fusion-party lines (New York, Connecticut) are not credited to the major party they endorse, which is how MEDSL publishes them. Row dates are election days and certified returns are not revised, so revisions are declared none.
attempts.run_note: CORRECTION (2026-09-16, before any holdout was scored): five district-cycles have a negative party receipts total, because a weball cycle total can be negative when a candidate refunds more than they raise. worldmodel.models.elections requires a nonnegative amount and refused to fit at all, so the loader clamps a negative party total to zero and counts the clamps in construction.clamped. AL-05 2014, FL-19 2012, MD-07 2022, TN-06 2016 and TN-06 2022 are affected. No result existed when this was corrected.

delinquency_rate.description: Unchanged from default_hazard.fdic_laus_quarterly: 100 * sum(bank_noncurrent_loans) / sum(bank_net_loans) over all FDIC-insured banks in the quarter, the bank-panel alternative requirements.json names for the unpublished FRED DRCCLACBS credit-card delinquency rate.

unemployment_rate.description: No longer a substitution: the rebuilt bls_labor publishes the national CPS unemployment rate (LNS14000000, 943 monthly observations 1948-2026) that the earlier partial build omitted, so the declared series is used directly instead of the constructed LAUS state aggregate.

attempts.data: fdic_bank_financials@6283087f + bls_labor@ffd7f43a (LNS14000000) + fred_policy_rate@2a3197b9, quarterly 2010Q1 onward
attempts.rationale: Removes one of the two substitutions behind the only passing default_hazard attempt, with the same splits so the two are directly comparable. The open question this attempt exists to settle: fdic_laus_quarterly passed with unemployment_sensitivity = +2.19 while default_hazard.fred_primary_realtime, on the declared DRCCLACBS and UNRATE series, produced -1.26. If the sign flips with the published national CPS rate, the disagreement was the constructed unemployment series; if it persists, it is the delinquency measure, and the passing attempt cannot be read as validating the declared mechanism.

unemployment_rate.description: Unchanged from v1: 100 * sum(unemployed) / sum(labor_force) over the 51 seasonally adjusted LAUS state series, now read from the completed bls_labor build.

attempts.data: fdic_bank_financials@6283087f + bls_labor@ffd7f43a + fred_policy_rate@2a3197b9, quarterly 2010Q1 onward
attempts.rationale: Version-only rerun. bls_labor@50917b81 came from an incomplete download holding 18.2M of 60.9M rows (about 30%), so the LAUS state aggregate behind the only passing attempt was built on a third of the data. Splits, criteria, overrides and loader options are identical; the dataset version is the only change.
attempts.run_note: RUN NOTE (2026-09-16, after the run): the declared data string named fred_policy_rate@2a3197b9, the version v1 used. Only bls_labor was pinned in the loader options, so the unpinned datasets resolved to latest and the run actually read fred_policy_rate@966a0099. Two dataset versions therefore changed, not one. Every parameter and every test metric reproduced v1 to the printed precision, which is itself evidence that neither rebuild changed the values used.

attempts.data: fred_cpi@c92b26cd (CPIAUCSL ALFRED vintages) + fred_policy_rate@2a3197b9 + bls_labor@ffd7f43a (LAUS states)
attempts.rationale: Version-only rerun of the second-wave Okun-proxy attempt on the completed bls_labor, for the same reason as default_hazard.fdic_laus_quarterly_v2. The attempt remains superseded by monetary_model.fred_realtime_v2, which uses the declared GDPC1/GDPPOT gap; it is rerun only to record whether the interim build changed its verdict.
attempts.run_note: RUN NOTE (2026-09-16, after the run): as above, the unpinned inputs resolved to latest, so the run read fred_cpi@34fe03f5 and fred_policy_rate@966a0099 rather than the c92b26cd and 2a3197b9 the declaration named. population.description: Monthly national population (Board of Governors/BEA POPTHM on FRED), aggregated to annual with the declared 'last' rule so an annual point is that year's December level. requirements.json names POPTHM as a source for this series alongside Census PEP; it is a total-resident-population measure rather than the PEP July-1 estimate, and it is rebased at each decennial census exactly as PEP is.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (POPTHM), monthly 1959-01..2026-07 with 325 ALFRED vintages from 1999-07-30, aggregated to annual
attempts.rationale: population_growth_rate.census_pep failed minimum_test_forecasts with n=4 because the published PEP vintages covered only 2010-2024. calibration-status.md named POPTHM ALFRED vintages as the fix and they are already published in fred_macro_panel: 811 monthly periods and 325 real vintages, the earliest 1999-07-30. Under the strict policy the first usable annual origin is therefore 2000, so the splits are taken from vintage coverage alone: train to 2005, validation 2006-2009, holdout 2010-2025 (16 annual forecasts against a declared minimum of 8). The cutoff stops at 2026-06-30 so the incomplete 2026 annual period is never aggregated.
attempts.expected_limits: A longer window with real vintages is a harder test, not an easier one: it spans the 2010 and 2020 census rebasings, each of which moves the level discontinuously, and beats_persistence_dm now has 16 forecasts to fail on rather than 4. interval_coverage failed at 0.50 on n=4 and is not addressed here; the interval method is left at its default so the only change is the panel.

attempts.data: census_population@normalized, extended with PEP national/state vintage files 2004-2007, 2011-2019 and 2025 and the 2000-2010 national intercensal series (annual national July-1 population 2000-2025, twelve vintages)
attempts.rationale: The declared primary source, on a longer panel. census_population now carries every PEP national/state ALLDATA vintage file the Census server still serves (V2004-V2007, V2011-V2025) plus the 2000-2010 national intercensal series, so national annual coverage runs 2000-2025 instead of 2010-2024 and there are twelve vintages instead of two. Availability is still the HTTP Last-Modified of each published file, which for every file older than the 2016 site migration is 2016-07-19 or later rather than its original December release date; that is an upper bound, so it delays availability and cannot leak. It does mean the first origin with the eight observations the component needs is 2016 (vintage 2015, 2016-09-01, with the intercensal series available from 2016-08-24). Splits are taken from that coverage: train to 2015, validation 2016, holdout 2017-2025 (9 annual forecasts against a declared minimum of 8).
attempts.expected_limits: Nine forecasts only just clears the declared minimum, and every one of them sits inside a single PEP vintage era plus the 2020 rebasing. The 2016 migration timestamps are the binding constraint: with the true December release dates the same files would give origins back to 2012. interval_coverage (0.50 on the four-forecast run) is not addressed.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (SNDR, 65 monthly periods 2021-04..2026-08 with 64 vintages) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF), monthly
attempts.rationale: The declared series, with the splits recut to the minimum the declared criteria demand. SNDR cannot be extended backwards -- the series does not exist before 2021-04 -- but the published panel now holds 65 months, and the component needs 36 to fit and 24 holdout forecasts. The split rule is mechanical and outcome-free: train is exactly the first 36 months (2021-04..2024-03), the holdout is the last 25 (2024-08..2026-08, one more than the declared minimum), and validation is the four months left in between. v1 declared a twelve-month validation window and was left with 17 origins against 24.
attempts.expected_limits: The holdout is a single easing cycle, so beats_persistence_dm (p = 0.871 on v1's 16 forecasts) is likely to fail again: a national deposit rate is close to a random walk at monthly frequency. interval_coverage was 0.438 on v1. Clearing minimum_test_forecasts makes those two verdicts real rather than unevaluable; it does not make them pass.
attempts.run_note: RUN NOTE (2026-09-17, after the run): the rationale predicted 25 holdout forecasts from the declared boundaries; the realized count is 24, because the first target after validation_end has no informative origin (its anchor's first publication already covers it). 24 is exactly the declared minimum, so minimum_test_forecasts passes with no margin. The split boundaries are as declared and were not changed.

deposit_rate.description: SUBSTITUTION, not the declared series. FDIC National Rate on Non-Jumbo Deposits (less than $100,000): Savings, weekly 2009-05-18..2021-03-29, aggregated to monthly with the declared 'mean' rule. This is SNDR's direct predecessor from the same FDIC National Rates programme, discontinued in 2021 when FDIC changed the methodology from a simple average over a sampled branch panel to a deposit-weighted average over all institutions. The level and the pass-through are therefore NOT comparable with SNDR's, and a pass here is a pass on SAVNRNJ.

attempts.data: fred_deposit_rates@normalized (SAVNRNJ, 624 weekly observations, ALFRED vintages from 2014-03-10) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF), monthly
attempts.rationale: SNDR starts 2021-04 and cannot be extended backwards, so the only way to give this component a real holdout is a different deposit rate. SAVNRNJ is the closest published object: the same FDIC programme, the same deposit product, 143 months of coverage. ALFRED vintages of SAVNRNJ begin 2014-03-10, so under the strict policy the first usable origin is 2014-04; splits are taken from that coverage with validation starting after it. Train 2009-05..2015-12 (80 months), validation 2016-2017, holdout 2018-01..2021-03 (39 forecasts). The holdout contains the 2019 cuts and the March 2020 collapse to the floor, which is the variation a pass-through parameter is supposed to explain.
attempts.expected_limits: This is a substituted series and must never be read as the declared SNDR component passing, exactly as default_hazard.fdic_laus_quarterly's pass on a substituted delinquency series is not read as default_hazard passing. The FDIC national rate is administered and sticky near zero for most of 2009-2015, so the fitted long-run pass-through describes a floor-bound regime.

deposit_rate.description: SUBSTITUTION, not the declared series. M2 Own Rate (FRED M2OWN, discontinued 2019-06): the weighted average interest rate paid on the deposit components of M2, monthly 1959-02..2019-06. It is an aggregate realised cost of deposits rather than an advertised retail rate, so it is a different object from SNDR and from SAVNRNJ; a pass here is a pass on the M2 own rate.

attempts.data: fred_deposit_rates@normalized (M2OWN, 10,515 vintage observations over 725 monthly periods, ALFRED vintages from 2014-03-07) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF), monthly
attempts.rationale: The second substitute, registered at the same time as the first and for the opposite reason: SAVNRNJ is close to SNDR in construction but covers only a floor-bound decade, while M2OWN covers 1959-2019 and therefore many complete tightening and easing cycles. Its ALFRED vintages also begin 2014-03, so origins start 2014-04 and the splits follow coverage: train 1959-02..2015-12, validation 2016, holdout 2017-01..2019-06 (30 forecasts). Registering both makes the disagreement visible if the two substitutes give different pass-through signs, which is how default_hazard's two variants were read.
attempts.expected_limits: M2OWN is revised (118 vintages for some periods), so the scored error carries revisions the origin could not see, which is the mechanism that made credit_growth's intervals too narrow. The interval method is left at its default, so interval_coverage may well fail from that direction. Substitution caveat as above.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@normalized (DPRIME) + fred_policy_rate@normalized (DFF), monthly means of daily vintages
attempts.diagnosis: v1 failed interval_coverage alone (0.988 against 0.80 +/- 0.15) while halving persistence's error at p = 0.0011. The predictive scale is an average across monetary-policy regimes, not a forecast of the current one. At the validation cutoff the in-sample residual scale is 0.2217 while the residual root mean square by decade is 0.1560 (1950s), 0.1796 (1960s), 0.2539 (1970s), 0.4186 (1980s), 0.1142 (1990s), 0.0816 (2000s) and 0.0416 (2010s) -- a tenfold spread, with the flat scale set mostly by the Volcker era. A 2005 ALFRED vintage of DPRIME publishes its history back to 1955, so the expanding in-sample scale carries that era into every forecast. This is visible before the holdout: in the SELECTION window (2013-2017, 59 forecasts) the default over-covers at 1.000 with a mean predictive sd of 0.2259 against a realized RMSE of 0.0498. The in-sample standardized errors also have kurtosis 6.0, which is what a rate that moves in discrete 25bp steps looks like: a spike at zero change with occasional jumps, not a Gaussian.
attempts.interval_method: empirical_trailing, window 120 months, 40 quantile nodes. The scale is the root mean square of the last 120 one-step residuals and the shape is the empirical quantiles of residuals standardized by their own trailing scale, so the discrete-step tails are taken from the data rather than assumed. No coefficient-uncertainty or revision component is declared: DPRIME is not revised and 746 residuals against 5 coefficients make x'Vx negligible, so neither is part of the diagnosis. Candidate interval methods are compared on the SELECTION window only (train_end -> validation_end, evaluated at validation_end, the same view validate_process uses to select candidates) and the declared rule is LOWEST VALIDATION-WINDOW CRPS, a proper score that is blind to interval coverage. Choosing the candidate whose coverage sits closest to 0.80 would be tuning to the acceptance criterion and was not used. Validation-window CRPS over the declared candidate grid (four methods x windows 36/60/120): gaussian_in_sample 0.05714; gaussian_trailing 0.02954 (36), 0.02945 (60), 0.02944 (120); student_t_trailing 0.03023 (60); empirical_trailing 0.02495 (36), 0.02497 (60), 0.02207 (120). The rule selects empirical_trailing at window 120, whose validation coverage (0.9153) is the WORST of the three trailing windows (0.8983 at 36, 0.8814 at 60) -- the evidence that CRPS and not coverage did the selecting.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits, vintage policy and acceptance criteria to interest_pass_through.fred_realtime; the predictive distribution is the only change, so the two attempts are directly comparable.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (PAYEMS, INDPRO across all index bases), monthly
attempts.correction: 2026-09-17: a scoring defect, not a re-specification. The backtest took the declared conditional input (INDPRO) at the target period from the evaluation vintage while its own lag in the same design row came from the origin's vintage, and the design reads industrial production only as the log ratio output_t/output_{t-1}. INDPRO is an index the Federal Reserve rebases and the published ALFRED vintages carry thirteen index bases, so that ratio was a rebasing factor rather than a growth rate: measured at the 2005-04 origin the regressor was -0.2177, a fabricated 22% collapse in industrial production, against a realized +0.0005 (95.3804 / 118.393 = 0.8056 is the base change). Every v1 and v2 forecast was computed with that shock in its design row, which is why their bias ran -2,172 thousand payrolls in 2005-2009 and decayed to zero as the origins approached the evaluation cutoff. labor_demand now declares conditional_rebase output: ratio, which carries the realized value onto the origin's base through the anchor-period overlap; this preserves the realized movement exactly and adds no information the origin did not have. The six other conditional inputs in the catalog were measured and declare 'none', so no other attempt changes.
attempts.diagnosis: Records what the correction alone does, with the predictive distribution left at its default, so the effect of the correction and the effect of any interval change stay separable. In the SELECTION window the correction moves MAE from 2,194.6 to 578.1 thousand payrolls, bias from -2,171.8 to +280.8 and the Diebold-Mariano p-value against persistence from 1.0000 to 0.0865.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits, vintage policy and acceptance criteria to labor_demand.fred_realtime_v2; the conditional-input scoring correction is the only change. Registered as a new attempt rather than a rerun because v1 and v2 keep their recorded numbers.
attempts.superseded_reason: WS-E interval calibration, 2026-09-17: see the sixth_wave note and docs/research-log/ws-e-interval-coverage.md.

attempts.data: fred_macro_panel@7dcce89c (PAYEMS, INDPRO across all index bases), monthly
attempts.diagnosis: With the conditional-input correction in force (v3) the remaining interval defect is the one credit_growth had: under the strict real-time policy the forecast is anchored on the PAYEMS level available at the origin while the actual is the latest vintage available at the evaluation cutoff, so the scored error carries the anchor's later benchmark revision, which is part of no in-sample residual. Measured at the validation cutoff, PAYEMS log revisions from first release to latest have a root mean square of 0.00458 for 2000s periods against a model residual scale of 0.00304 -- the revision component is larger than the residual it is being added to. In the SELECTION window the default under-covers at 0.600 with a mean predictive sd of 414.5 thousand against a realized RMSE of 767.2, and standardized errors have root mean square 1.86.
attempts.interval_method: gaussian_in_sample residual scale plus an independent data-revision component: the standard deviation of the log revisions the publisher has ALREADY made by the origin, over the most recent 120 mature periods, where mature means at least 24 months old. Twenty-four months is the age at which a CES period has been through both its level benchmark (published with January data each February, revising from the previous March forward) and the following year's seasonal-factor revision. Ten years keeps the estimate inside the current benchmark methodology instead of averaging over the 1950s, whose log-revision root mean square is 0.0185 against 0.0046 in the 2000s. The mean revision is reported and deliberately not used to shift the point forecast, so systematic revision bias stays visible in the bias statistic. Candidate interval methods are compared on the SELECTION window only (train_end -> validation_end, evaluated at validation_end, the same view validate_process uses to select candidates) and the declared rule is LOWEST VALIDATION-WINDOW CRPS, a proper score that is blind to interval coverage. Choosing the candidate whose coverage sits closest to 0.80 would be tuning to the acceptance criterion and was not used. Validation-window CRPS over the declared candidates: default 440.1; +revision 431.0; gaussian_trailing(60) 489.5; gaussian_trailing(60)+revision 437.5; gaussian_trailing(120)+revision 437.6; empirical_trailing(60)+revision 434.9; empirical_trailing(120)+revision 437.0. The rule selects the revision component alone. The heteroskedasticity argument that fixed interest_pass_through is real here too (residual root mean square 0.0065 in the 1940s against 0.0011 in the 1990s) but points the other way: a trailing scale NARROWS this interval (mean sd 206.1 against 414.5) and drives validation coverage down to 0.358, so it is not adopted.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits, vintage policy and acceptance criteria to labor_demand.fred_realtime_v3.

attempts.data: bls_labor@ffd7f43a2761 (QCEW annual averages, private ownership, state x NAICS sector, 2005-2024)
attempts.diagnosis: v1 failed interval_coverage from below (0.597) while beating the year-effect-only baseline at p = 1.2e-04. The defect is in the predictive variance of a random effect, and it is demonstrable from the forecast-error decomposition without reference to any coverage number. The forecast is mean-of-Y-observed-year-effects + b x shock; the actual is next year's own year effect + b x shock + residual. The error therefore contains (next year's effect - the mean of Y past effects), whose variance is between + between/Y = between x (1 + 1/Y). per_unit_year_mean prices only between/Y, the sampling variance of the mean, which is the right variance for a year effect that is a fixed level being estimated -- and that contradicts the existence of a between-year variance in the first place. So per_unit_year_mean's per-region within-year scale was a correction and its common term was an error.
attempts.interval_method: per_unit_year_draw: the per-region within-year residual variance of per_unit_year_mean (each region's own residual mean square shrunk toward the pooled one by a single prior observation, declared because region residual sds span a factor of fifty) paired with the fresh-draw common term between x (1 + 1/Y) of the pooled default. The test that this is a correction and not tuning: it is ONE change applied for one reason to BOTH regional panels, and it moves them in OPPOSITE directions relative to their thresholds -- it widens, so it can only help qcew's under-coverage (0.597) and can only hurt cbp's over-coverage (0.980). A change tuned to a threshold cannot do that.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits, entity rule and acceptance criteria to regional_model.qcew_state_sectors.
attempts.expected_limits: no_revision_leakage fails structurally and no interval method can change it: no published employment source in this catalog carries vintages, so QCEW row dates are not information times. The attempt can at best reduce its failing criteria from two to one.
attempts.entity_rule: Every state-equivalent QCEW publishes at aggregation level 54 (50 states, DC and Puerto Rico; 53 areas), and every two-digit NAICS private sector. Selection is availability only.

attempts.data: census_business@5b0995c7 (County Business Patterns employment by state and NAICS sector)
attempts.diagnosis: Run for the same reason as qcew_state_sectors_v2 and with the same single change, to show that the change is applied for its stated reason and not to a threshold. v2 over-covers at 0.980; a wider common term can only make that worse, and it is registered and run anyway.
attempts.rationale: Identical data, splits and acceptance criteria to regional_model.cbp_state_sectors_v2.
attempts.expected_limits: interval_coverage is expected to fail WORSE than v2. With one holdout year all 51 forecasts share one draw of the common component, so coverage here is one Bernoulli trial and not a coverage estimate; no_revision_leakage also fails, as CBP publishes no vintages.

not_run.note: voteview_rollcalls publishes roll_call_member_positions for Congresses 110-119 (e.g. Senate 117: 949 roll calls), so the data exist. The ideal-point MAP refit at every holdout origin exceeds the declared 30-minute budget per attempt.
Daily closes are available; the grid SMM fit at every window origin exceeds the declared budget.

blocked_on_data: See worldmodel.estimation.loaders.availability(): BLOCKED_COMPONENTS and BLOCKED_FAMILIES name the exact missing series and the dataset that must publish them. As of the fifth wave the elections family is no longer blocked (mit_election_returns published House district returns) and regional has a long panel (bls_labor QCEW). What remains blocked is field_diffusion_transport (epa_aqs_daily), bilateral_flow_gravity (freight FAF5), trade (cepii_baci) and influence (no unit-period exposure panel).
rerun: python3 -m worldmodel calibrate-all   (add --attempt ID to rerun one attempt, --no-publish to skip artifact publication)
second_wave: 2026-09-15, after fred_cpi (full ALFRED vintages) and bls_labor (current vintage) were published: two further attempts were pre-registered below with their splits before any holdout was scored. fred_macro_panel had acquired but not published a normalized output, so GDPC1, GDPPOT, INDPRO, FEDFUNDS, TOTALSL, RRSFS, DPRIME, SNDR, DPSACBW027SBOG and DRCCLACBS were still unavailable.
third_wave: 2026-09-15, after fred_macro_panel published 7.57M records covering every required FRED series with full ALFRED vintages (realtime_start/realtime_end on every observation). Nine attempts below were pre-registered with their splits before any holdout was scored. Splits start inside each series vintage era, because under the strict policy nothing is visible before a series first entered ALFRED: DFF and DPRIME 2005-06, DPSACBW027SBOG 2012-08, DRCCLACBS 2011-05, RRSFS 2001-06, TOTALSL and FEDFUNDS 1996-12, GDPC1 1992-12, GDPPOT 1994-01, SNDR 2021-04. The two second-wave attempts that used substitute series are superseded but retained with their verdicts so the substitution history stays visible.
fourth_wave: 2026-09-15, after the chained-dollar base-year bug was fixed and fred_macro_panel and fred_cpi were rebuilt (panel 7dcce89c, cpi 34fe03f5). Every observation now carries attributes.source_units, a per-vintage unit_multiplier and base_period, and the unit token is per vintage. Two input defects were corrected: 189 of 849 panel series changed units across vintages (the old build labelled every vintage with one unit), and TOTALSL was published in billions for some vintages and millions for others, so 11,612 of its 13,537 values changed (e.g. 1998-03 1.3322 -> 1332.2). Five attempts are re-registered below with the SAME splits as their v1 counterparts so the two are comparable; the v1 verdicts are kept and marked contaminated. Verified value-identical between the two builds, so their verdicts stand without a rerun: DPRIME, DFF, SNDR, DRCCLACBS, UNRATE, DPSACBW027SBOG, PAYEMS, FEDFUNDS and RRSFS (RRSFS changed only its unit token).
fifth_wave: 2026-09-16. Three strands. (a) Interval calibration on the three attempts that beat their baselines on point accuracy and failed ONLY interval_coverage: inventory_balance (0.640), credit_growth (0.596) and regional_model (1.000). Each was diagnosed first, and each new attempt records the diagnosis and the interval method it declares; the diagnoses differ, so the methods differ. Predictive distributions are now a declared choice in the estimator (worldmodel/estimation/intervals.py: gaussian_in_sample, gaussian_trailing, student_t_trailing, empirical_trailing, with optional coefficient-uncertainty and data-revision components; regional: pooled_year_draw or per_unit_year_mean), not a tuned multiplier, and the default keeps every earlier run bit-identical. (b) elections_model is no longer blocked: mit_election_returns published 33,805 U.S. House district rows, so the family is scored on real district returns with the split taken by election year. (c) bls_labor was rebuilt from 18.2M to 60.9M rows (the earlier build was an incomplete download), so every attempt that read it is rerun with the version as the only change, the newly available national CPS unemployment rate replaces one of the two substitutions in the passing default_hazard attempt, and QCEW makes the long regional panel possible.
panel_length_wave: 2026-09-17 (WS-D, panel length). Two attempts failed minimum_test_forecasts, which is a data-quantity failure and not a modelling one: population_growth_rate.census_pep had 14 annual observations and n=4 against a declared 8, and deposit_rate_pass_through.fred_realtime had 62 monthly observations and n=16 against a declared 24. Five attempts are registered below and every split is taken from data coverage alone. Population is attempted twice: on the declared primary source, with census_population extended from two PEP vintages to twelve (V2004-V2007, V2011-V2025, plus the 2000-2010 national intercensal series, so annual national coverage is 2000-2025 instead of 2010-2024); and on POPTHM, which requirements.json already names as a source for the same series and which fred_macro_panel already publishes with 325 ALFRED vintages back to 1999-07-30. The deposit rate cannot be extended backwards -- SNDR does not exist before 2021-04 -- so it is attempted three ways: the declared series with the splits recut to the minimum the criteria demand (train = exactly the 36 months needed to fit, holdout = the last 25 months, validation = what is left), and two SUBSTITUTE series in a new fred_deposit_rates dataset (SAVNRNJ, SNDR's discontinued predecessor from the same FDIC programme, 2009-2021; and M2OWN, the M2 own rate, 1959-2019). Both substitutions are declared as overrides and neither can be read as the declared SNDR component passing, following the precedent of default_hazard.fdic_laus_quarterly.
sixth_wave: 2026-09-17, WS-E. interval_coverage blocked 16 of the 35 attempts, more than any other criterion, and needs no new data. Each of the 16 was diagnosed separately into one of two causes the record already distinguishes: a SCORING BUG (a real-time forecast graded against a later vintage, as credit_growth was) or GENUINE MISCALIBRATION (the predictive distribution is the wrong shape or the wrong width for the right reason). One new scoring bug was found and fixed in the code: the backtest handed a declared conditional input's value at the target period from the evaluation vintage while its own lag in the same design row came from the origin's vintage, so labor_demand's output-growth regressor was the INDPRO rebasing factor (-0.2177) rather than realized growth (+0.0005). Components now declare conditional_rebase per input; only labor_demand declares one, and the other six conditional inputs were measured and left unchanged. The regional family gains per_unit_year_draw, which pairs per_unit_year_mean's per-region within-year scale with the fresh-draw common term the default already used, because between/Y is the predictive variance of a year effect treated as a fixed level and the forecast error contains next year's own draw. Every candidate interval method was compared on the SELECTION window under a declared rule of lowest CRPS -- a proper score, blind to coverage -- and no threshold was relaxed. Attempts with no principled fix are recorded as still failing: see docs/research-log/ws-e-interval-coverage.md for the count and the reason for each.
